- Integration surface: server-to-server calls from Crestline backend to Redwood (generation + embeddings + reranker).
- Constraints: Crestline wants centralized key control, automated rotation, and scoped credentials per environment (staging/prod).

2) Rotation cadence and audit logs (SOC2 evidence);
3) Whether Redwood supports short-lived tokens obtained from Crestline Vault/KMS;
4) Structured output + tool-calling patterns for referring to internal systems.

Hi Asha — thanks, great context. Summary of a recommended architecture that lines up with Redwood capabilities and your Vault plan: 

Recommended auth topology (server-to-server):
- Primary: OAuth2 Client Credentials (server) for lifecycle-managed clients. Client credentials issued by Crestline Vault -> exchanged for Redwood tokens via an authorization handshake.
- Alternative / complement: Service account JWTs minted by Crestline (short TTL, e.g., 15m) and signed by your KMS/HSM. Redwood accepts signed JWTs and returns a scoped session token.
- For CLI/ops: Ephemeral API keys created via an internal Vault role for humans with 1h TTL. No long-lived API keys in prod.

Rotation & revocation:
- Recommend 15m–1h short-lived session tokens for runtime calls; rotate client secrets monthly (automated via Vault).
- Redwood emits token issue / token usage logs including: token_id (hashed), client_id, scope, issue_ts, user_agent, request_path, ingest_region. We can produce a SOC2-friendly export (s3/secure bucket) of these logs for audit.

SDK & integration notes (quick snippet):
- SDK bootstrapping (Node example):

const token = await vault.get('redwood/session', {role: 'crestline-app'});
const client = new Redwood({ auth: { type: 'bearer', token } });
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'xlarge-beta', prompt: 'Summarize chart...' });

- Header pattern Redwood expects (server-to-server):
Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-session-token>
X-Redwood-Client: crestline-backend
X-Request-Trace: <uuid>

Embeddings / reranker notes:
- We recommend one embeddings API keyspace per environment. Use an index-per-tenant approach; we support per-index ACLs.
- Reranker: run reranker as a separate endpoint with rerank-scopes so embeddings and generation tokens are accounted for separately (helps cost attribution).

Structured output & tool-calling:
- For PHI-sensitive calls, use structured output with explicit metadata fields (schema enforced by Redwood) and our tool-calling bridge that can call a Crestline internal webhook (signed by mutual TLS). This allows you to keep raw PHI inside Crestline and only send redacted/structured tokens to Redwood when required.

Workshop agenda suggestion (60m):
1) Auth handshake patterns (15m)
2) SDK bootstrap + Vault demo (20m)
3) Routing & environment scoping (10m)
4) Q&A + next steps & SOW checklist (15m)

I’ll attach a one-page diagram and a short sample MAP for procurement.
